title: When Both Sides Adapt: The Challenges of Evaluating Interactive LLM Systems
abstract: arXiv:2611.17239v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: In interactive systems where users engage with LLMs, users are adaptive and, after observing LLM responses, can change their prompting strategy, as well as the type and difficulty of subsequent tasks. Thus model responses can influence the set of prompts on which the model is subsequently evaluated. We study the implications of this user adaptivity and prompt endogeneity for the evaluation of LLMs. We define two classes of estimands for comparing models: the common-distribution effect, which compares model performance on the same distribution of prompts, and the induced-distribution effect, which compares each model on the prompt distribution generated through user interaction. We show that offline benchmark evaluation and live A/B testing target different quantities, with the standard difference-in-means estimators for the two methods converging to the common-distribution effect and the induced-distribution effect, respectively. translated_title: 当双方都在适应时：评估交互式LLM系统的挑战
translated_abstract: 在用户与LLM交互的系统中，用户是具有适应性的：在观察到LLM的响应后，用户可以改变自己的提示策略，以及后续任务的类型和难度。因此，模型的响应会影响模型随后被评估时所使用的提示集合。我们研究了这种用户适应性和提示内生性对LLM评估的影响。我们定义了两类用于比较模型的估计量：共同分布效应，它比较模型在相同提示分布上的表现；以及诱导分布效应，它比较每个模型在通过用户交互所产生的提示分布上的表现。我们证明，离线基准评估和在线A/B测试针对的是不同的量，两种方法的标准均值差估计量分别收敛于共同分布效应和诱导分布效应。
tldr: 该论文揭示了用户适应性与提示内生性给LLM评估带来的挑战，证明离线基准测试与在线A/B测试分别收敛于“共同分布效应”和“诱导分布效应”这两种本质上不同的比较目标。
en_tdlr: This paper shows that user adaptivity and prompt endogeneity complicate LLM evaluation, proving that offline benchmarking and live A/B testing converge to fundamentally different estimands—the common-distribution effect and the induced-distribution effect, respectively.
